speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the prematurity and immediate onset of distress, is there any history of meconium aspiration, and have you noticed cyanosis or grunting respirations? Also, has a chest X-ray or blood gas analysis been performed yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: Blood_Gases: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L. Chest_Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs.

*Note: Based on the provided data, the clinical presentation (respiratory distress, grunting, retractions, cyanosis) combined with the imaging findings is more consistent with Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity. Tuberculosis is highly unlikely in a 2-hour-old newborn with these specific radiographic patterns and acute onset following premature labor, unless there was a rare congenital case or maternal transmission with prior incubation, which would present differently.*

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity. The combination of 33-week gestation, immediate onset of distress, elevated PaCO2, and the characteristic "ground glass" appearance on the chest X-ray confirms this diagnosis. I will initiate treatment with surfactant therapy and respiratory support immediately.
